name: Absent Rector
description: Minor church Hook: the priest who collects the benefice does not live in the parish, and his duties fall to a curate.

name: Incompetent Curate
description: Minor church Hook: the church's curate is incompetent and, if discovered, may be removed, bringing many visitations; not available to a major church.

name: Vast Sanctuary
description: Minor church Hook: by custom anyone may seek sanctuary within a wide area around the church, often putting the priest in conflict with the sheriff.

name: Urban (Church Hook)
description: Church Hook taken by the example Urban Parish located in a large town.

name: Protector (Church Hook)
description: Church Hook under which the church canons must protect a group, such as a town's Jewish minority, from persecution.

name: Crumbling
description: Church Hook for a church that is very old and in a bad state of repair.

name: Faerie Court (Church Hook)
description: Church Hook for a church troubled by a nearby faerie court whose lords cast spells causing its decay.

name: Flickering Aura
description: Church Hook under which the church's Divine aura drops (e.g. to 3 for a year) unless certain rites, such as carrying relics on the perambulation, are observed.

name: Fallen Temple
description: Church Hook for a church or chapel built on the site of a former pagan temple.

name: Spies
description: Church Hook in which someone in the church, such as the parish clerk, secretly reports on the priest to the bishop.

name: Chapter of Canons
description: Church Boon giving the church a body of canons.

name: Edifice
description: Church Boon representing a notable building feature, such as a church tower.

name: Local Ally
description: Church Boon representing a local ally, such as a town guild master.

name: Minority (Church Boon)
description: Church Boon representing a minority community, such as Jews, attached to the parish.

name: Powerful Ally
description: Church Boon representing a powerful patron, such as a bishop related to the curate.

name: Chase
description: Church Boon associated with a former hunting estate forest used by the parish.

name: Burial Rights
description: Church Boon granting the church the right to bury the dead.

name: Seclusion
description: Church Boon for a church in a secluded location, such as a covenant chapel in a shaded glen.

name: Urban Parish
description: Example church in one of the larger towns of a diocese, with canons, a guild altar, a Jewish minority, and a Divine aura of 5.

name: Village Parish
description: Example crumbling old church serving three villages beside a forest haunted by a faerie court, with a Divine aura of 4.

name: Covenant Chapel
description: Example chapel built in a glen near a covenant tower on the site of a pagan temple, with a Divine aura of 3.

name: Saint's Thigh Bone
description: A relic with Faith Score 3 and a Cure Blindness power, kept at the example Covenant Chapel.

name: Divine Aura
description: The supernatural aura of the Divine present at churches, rated by level (e.g. 3 to 5 for example churches).

name: Relic
description: Holy objects held by churches, with a Faith Score and powers; minor relics have Faith Score 1.

name: Faith Score
description: The rating of a relic's holy power.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power found in vis sources, such as pawns of Creo from Easter bells or Imaginem from mid-summer dawn light.

name: Creo
description: Hermetic Technique; a church vis source yields Creo vis from the pealing bells at Easter Mass.

name: Animal
description: Hermetic Form; a village parish yields Animal vis from the first boar of the hunt.

name: Imaginem
description: Hermetic Form; a village parish yields Imaginem vis from mid-summer dawn light in the bell tower.

name: Rego
description: Hermetic Technique; a Rego Animal enchanted box could transport letters between a covenant and an enclosed religious.

name: Bible
description: Holy scripture held by churches and copied by monks.

name: Missal
description: Liturgical book held by the example parish churches.

name: Parish Register
description: Book (Level 7) held by the example Village Parish.

name: Breviary
description: Liturgical book (Quality 6) held by the example Covenant Chapel.

name: Psalter
description: Book of psalms that most monks know by heart and that is read during meals.

name: Miracula
description: Monastic chronicles containing ghost stories of souls returned from purgatory and miracles of saints, read to foster Devotion and useful for research.

name: Mirabilia
description: Monastic books recording faeries and magical or unusual natural phenomena, signs and wonders; a research resource for magi.

name: Religious Life
description: The vocation of monks and nuns; 'religious' is the technical term for monks and nuns, who observe the canonical hours, prayer and service to God.

name: Rule of Saint Benedict
description: The most widespread monastic rule in Mythic Europe, laying down detailed regulations and a daily timetable for monks and nuns; most religious orders follow variants of it.

name: Rule of Saint Augustine
description: Monastic rule followed by Augustinian canons, Premonstratensians and many canonesses; fashionable after 1215.

name: Statutes of Saint Bruno
description: The rule followed by the Carthusians instead of the Rule of Benedict.

name: Ancrene Riwle
description: The anchoress' rule, written in England in the early 13th century for three anchoresses, based on monastic rules but adapted to the anchoress' enclosed life.

name: Monastic Vows
description: The three chief vows of chastity, poverty (humility) and obedience sworn as solemn oaths by almost all religious after a year's novitiate.

name: Novice
description: A junior member of a monastery or nunnery serving a probationary year before taking vows.

name: Oblate
description: A child given to a monastery to be raised and educated; the practice was outlawed by the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215.

name: Fourth Lateran Council
description: Church council of 1215 that outlawed oblates and required all religious communities to adopt an approved rule.

name: Tonsure
description: The ring of hair left when a monk's head is shaved on taking vows.

name: Divine Office
description: The daily prayers recited at the canonical hours, also called the Opus Dei or Liturgy of the Hours.

name: Matins
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: First service of the day at midnight, the monks roused by the sacristan's bell.

name: Lauds
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: Service at 1 am (or dawn in summer) after which monks return to bed.

name: Prime
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: Service at 7 am when monks are roused from bed.

name: Terce
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: Morning service at 9 am, followed by the chapter meeting.

name: Sext
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: Midday service.

name: Nones
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: Afternoon service at 3 pm.

name: Vespers
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: 5 pm service marking the end of the day's labors.

name: Compline
description: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: Evening service at 7 pm, after which monks retire to bed.

name: Mass
description: The central Church rite, celebrated by a priest for monks, servants and lay folk.

name: Sign Language (Monastery)
description: Ability covering the silent sign languages monks use when speech is forbidden; each monastery's version defaults with penalties to other houses and orders.

name: Monastic Gardens
description: Monastic horticulture including cloister garth, orchards, physic garden, infirmary garden and herbers.

name: Infirmary
description: Room or detached building of a monastery where sick, elderly and indigent people are cared for by the monks.

name: Chapterhouse
description: Monastic building where monks gather for readings and where the abbot consults the community.

name: Scriptorium
description: Monastic room where books are copied, overseen by the chancellor.

name: Beguinage
description: The home of a group of beguines living together; an urban establishment requiring the bishop's approval.

name: Anchorhold
description: The cell of an anchoress, usually attached to a church with a window onto the altar and another onto the street.

name: Visitation
description: Periodic inspection of churches and nunneries by a bishop or his deputy, documenting faults.

name: Sanctuary
description: Protection customarily granted to those who seek refuge within a church's bounds.

name: Devotion
description: Religious fervor fostered by reading miracula and similar works.

name: Christian Mysticism
description: Mystical state understood as a form of prayer imparting direct personal knowledge of God, with rules for play.

name: Apostasy
description: Abandoning religious life; considered the worst sin, with fugitive nuns hunted and returned to the cloister.

name: Sin
description: Wrongdoing exploited by Tempters; vanity, greed and lust are less serious than pride, while apostasy is worst.

name: Reputation
description: A character's standing, such as an abbess's reputation of level 4 or a mystic's reputation spreading through a diocese.

name: Arcane Connection
description: A magical link to a target; a runaway novice's clothes, or a nun as a bride of Christ, might serve as one.

name: The Gift
description: The magical talent of magi that provokes suspicion from abbots and hostillars; a Gifted nun is shunned in her nunnery.

name: Twilight
description: Hermetic magical state; a Twilight-addled magus plots to use a nun as an Arcane Connection to God.

name: Regio
description: A supernatural region; the covenant of Cunfin hides in one, and an anchoress' cell might give access to one.

name: Divine
description: The Realm of God, source of mystics' visions and church auras.

name: Infernal
description: Realm of demons and Tempters that spread sin in nunneries.

name: Faerie
description: Realm of faeries, represented by faerie courts haunting forests.

name: Church Lore
description: Knowledge of the Church, required of canons, abbots, precentors and all nuns.

name: Profession: Scribe
description: Profession held by church notaries.

name: Profession: Mason
description: Profession held by a master stonemason in a parish's specialists.

name: Brawl
description: Ability of churchwardens in the example Urban Parish.

name: Profession: Steward
description: Administrative skill useful to abbesses and terrars.

name: Leadership
description: Ability expected of abbots, abbesses and terrars.

name: Intrigue
description: Ability important to abbots, terrars and scholarly nuns.

name: Folk Ken
description: Ability useful to abbots, terrars, cellarers and heads of the novitiate.

name: Etiquette
description: Ability an abbot probably has, perhaps specialized in nobility or clergy.

name: Theology
description: Academic Ability useful for abbots and clerics advising nunneries.

name: Civil and Canon Law
description: Legal Ability useful to abbots and terrars.

name: Common Law
description: Legal knowledge needed by terrars in some regions.

name: Philosophiae
description: Academic Ability an abbot may have.

name: Dominion Lore
description: Knowledge of the Dominion that abbots and scholarly nuns may have.

name: Profession: Terrar
description: Profession of a monastery's land agent.

name: Profession: Reeve
description: Profession relevant to managing monastic estates.

name: Bargain
description: Ability useful to cellarers.

name: Profession: Cellaress
description: Profession of the nunnery official responsible for food and drink.

name: Chirurgy
description: Medical Ability required of an infirmarian.

name: Medicine
description: Academic medical Ability of monastic infirmarians.

name: Teaching
description: Ability for passing on knowledge, needed by precentors and heads of the novitiate.

name: Herbalism
description: Ability tied to the Herbalism Virtue, held by a nunnery's herbalist.

name: Profession: Apothecary
description: Profession held by a nunnery herbalist.

name: Awareness
description: Ability useful to a head of the novitiate monitoring novices.

name: Latin
description: Language all nuns are expected to know.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Academic Ability expected of all nuns and taught to novices.

name: Music
description: Ability required of a precentor.

name: Magic Theory
description: Hermetic Ability; scribes lacking it render copied Hermetic works worthless.

name: Understanding
description: Supernatural Ability associated with the Understanding power of True Faith mystics.

name: Senior Clergy
description: Social Status Virtue appropriate for abbots, abbesses and very powerful priors.

name: Religious (Social Status)
description: Social Status Virtue for priors, nuns, beguines and penitents who have taken religious life.

name: Temporal Influence
description: Virtue an abbot or abbess is likely to have.

name: Premonitions
description: Virtue; a cellaress with Premonitions of unexpected visitors could be entertaining.

name: Herbalism (Virtue)
description: Virtue giving access to the Herbalism Ability, held by a nunnery's herbalist.

name: Privileged Upbringing
description: Common Virtue for nuns from noble families.

name: Apt Student
description: Virtue enhancing learning, suitable for a scholarly nun.

name: Book Learner
description: Virtue enhancing learning from books, suitable for a scholarly nun.

name: Gentle Gift
description: Virtue that spares a Gifted girl the distrust The Gift normally causes in a nunnery.

name: Faerie Friend
description: Virtue that can make a girl too much trouble for her family, leading to a nunnery.

name: Ghostly Warder
description: Virtue that can lead a family to place a girl in a nunnery.

name: Strong Faerie Blood
description: Virtue that can give an unnatural appearance off-putting to suitors.

name: Giant Blood
description: Virtue that can give an unnatural appearance off-putting to suitors.

name: True Faith
description: Major Virtue; some mystics' visions derive from it.

name: Understanding (Virtue)
description: Major Virtue and Supernatural Power of Understanding associated with True Faith mystics.

name: Meditation
description: Major Virtue and Supernatural Method required for the Understanding power.

name: Monastic Vows (Flaw)
description: Story Flaw for religious characters living outside their community where keeping vows is a struggle.

name: Regular
description: Minor Flaw often appropriate for nuns.

name: Plagued by Supernatural Entity
description: Flaw that can make a girl too much trouble for her family.

name: Supernatural Nuisance
description: Flaw that can make a girl too much trouble for her family.

name: Crippled
description: Flaw making a woman unmarriageable and likely placed in a nunnery.

name: Disfigured
description: Flaw making a woman unmarriageable and likely placed in a nunnery.

name: Hunchback
description: Flaw making a woman unmarriageable and likely placed in a nunnery.

name: Tainted with Evil
description: Flaw that makes a nunnery reluctant to accept a girl.

name: Simple-Minded
description: Flaw; such characters may still be married off if attractive or wealthy.

name: Social Handicap
description: Flaw category that may lead a husband to send his wife to a nunnery.

name: Blatant Gift
description: Flaw; a poor nunnery might accept a girl with it for a generous endowment, and a maga with it may suit a hermit life.

name: Curse of Venus
description: Flaw hidden in a young nun until a younger confessor arrives.

name: Ability Block: Academic
description: Flaw covering the illiteracy of most beguines and penitents.

name: Visions
description: Flaw covering most religious mystics' experiences.

name: Monk
description: Male religious living under a rule in a monastery.

name: Nun
description: Female religious living under a rule in a nunnery, usually of noble birth and strictly enclosed.

name: Abbot
description: Ruler and spiritual father of a monastery, elected for life and often very powerful.

name: Abbess
description: Head of a larger nunnery, the most powerful position a woman can normally attain.

name: Prior
description: Second in command to the abbot, or head of a priory, handling administration and outside relations.

name: Terrar
description: A monastery's land agent responsible for estates, tithes and accounts.

name: Cellarer
description: Official responsible for provision of food and drink.

name: Bursar
description: Official combining cellarer and terrar in smaller houses, or keeping internal accounts in larger ones.

name: Infirmarian
description: Religious who cares for the sick and elderly and the health of the community.

name: Head of the Novitiate
description: Official responsible for those preparing to take religious vows.

name: Sacrist
description: Official responsible for vestments, candles, incense and upkeep of the church.

name: Sacristan
description: Monk who rouses the others with a bell for Matins.

name: Precentor
description: Monk responsible for music and chants.

name: Porter
description: Religious who answers the monastery door and receives gifts.

name: Hostillar
description: Monk in charge of the guest house, not bound by silence; most often dealt with by visitors.

name: Almoner
description: Monk responsible for distributing surplus food to beggars at the gate.

name: Chancellor
description: Monastic librarian overseeing the scriptorium and access to books.

name: Dean of Order
description: Monk, one per ten, responsible for keeping good order among his brethren.

name: Vicar
description: Priest appointed by a monastery to administer a parish it holds, paid a wage while the monastery takes the tithe.

name: Curate
description: Priest who performs a parish's duties on behalf of an absent rector.

name: Canon
description: Clergy of a church or cathedral chapter; examples specialize in Church Lore.

name: Canoness
description: Woman who takes vows of chastity and obedience under a rule, usually Augustinian, but may own property and is more urban and active than nuns.

name: Beguine
description: Pious laywoman living chastely in prayer and good works without formal vows, alone, with family or in a beguinage.

name: Beghard
description: A man living chastely following the beguine lifestyle.

name: Penitent
description: Woman living a permanent religious life of penitential practices in small groups, known as bizzoca, pinzocheri or continentes.

name: Anchoress
description: Woman enclosed in a cell attached to a church, respected and able to interact through her window, served by female servants.

name: Hermit
description: Holy recluse living alone; women living so may be suspected of witchcraft.

name: Mystic
description: Religious receiving visions and prophecy believed to come from God.

name: Principal Mistress
description: Woman selected annually to lead a large beguinage.

name: Herbalist
description: Nunnery official with the Herbalism Virtue who cultivates herbs.

name: Tempter
description: A kind of demon busy in nunneries, using those without real vocation to spread sin.

name: Redcap
description: Hermetic messenger; a traveling Redcap might discover a Gifted nun.

name: Quaesitores
description: Hermetic investigators whose attention covenants fear if links to nunneries are exposed.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi, which covenants must conceal from inquisitive clergy.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House; a story seed features a Jerbiton maga disguised as a penitent.

name: Infernalist
description: Diabolist; a story seed involves an Infernalist cult in a monastery.

name: Nitibus
description: A demon from Realms of Power: The Infernal usable as the Tempter who spirits away a nun.

name: Leap of Homecoming
description: Spell an anchoress might use to leave her cell for another location and later return.

name: The Church
description: The ecclesiastical institution of Mythic Europe that governs religious life and polices nuns and beguines.

name: Orthodox Church
description: Eastern Christian faith whose religious follow different traditions.

name: Benedictines
description: Religious order following the Rule of Saint Benedict, to which most monks in western Mythic Europe belong; its abbeys hold great wealth.

name: Cistercians
description: Monastic order that acknowledged nunneries only from 1213; detailed in Chapter 6.

name: Cluniacs
description: Monastic order detailed in Chapter 6: The Corrupt.

name: Vallumbrosans
description: Monastic order detailed in Chapter 6: The Corrupt.

name: Augustinian Canons
description: Regular clergy under the Rule of Saint Augustine found in cathedral chapters, known as Black Canons, generous in alms.

name: Carthusians
description: Austere order of monks and nuns following the Statutes of Saint Bruno, living in individual cells in complete silence.

name: Gilbertines
description: Double English order founded in 1130 at Sempringham by Saint Gilbert, with black habit and white cowl.

name: Premonstratensians
description: Order founded by Saint Norbert with 12 disciples, following the Rule of Augustine; converted the Wends and admits only monks since 1198.

name: Trinitarians
description: Order known as Red Friars, founded in 1198 in France to ransom Christian captives.

name: Carmelite Order
aliases: Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel
description: Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, originating from hermits on Mount Carmel in the Holy Land devoted to solitude and penance.

name: Franciscans
description: Mendicant order of friars, followers of Francis, the strongest new spiritual movement.

name: Templars
description: Military order discussed in Chapter 9.

name: Beguine Movement
description: New way of life for pious women arising in northern France, Flanders and Germany in the early 13th century.

name: Wends
description: People converted by the Premonstratensians.

name: Saint Benedict
description: Author of the Rule of Saint Benedict followed by most monks of western Mythic Europe.

name: Saint Augustine
description: Author of the Rule of Augustine; his writings inspired the first rules for nuns.

name: Saint Bruno
description: Author of the Statutes followed by the Carthusians.

name: Saint Gilbert
description: Founder of the Gilbertines, died 1190 and canonized 1202; feast on February 4th.

name: Saint Norbert
description: Founder of the Premonstratensians with 12 disciples.

name: Saint Alban
description: Martyr whose shrine inspired Christina of Markyate to vow virginity.

name: Samson
description: Example abbot addressed as 'Lord Abbot Samson'.

name: King John of England
description: King who intervened in the election of the abbot of Bury Saint Edmunds in 1210.

name: Robert of Arbrissel
description: Charismatic hermit and preacher who founded the Abbey of Fontrevrault in 1100.

name: Henry II
description: King of England interred at Fontrevrault; founded its daughter house at Amesbury.

name: Richard I
description: King of England interred at Fontrevrault.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Queen who spent her last ten years at Fontrevrault and was buried there in 1204.

name: Berthe
description: Abbess of Fontrevrault in 1220, in charge for two years.

name: Eleanor of England
description: Daughter of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine who married Alfonso VIII and co-founded Las Huelgas in 1187.

name: Alfonso VIII of Castile
description: King who with his wife Eleanor founded the nunnery of Las Huelgas near Burgos.

name: Constance
description: Daughter of Alfonso VIII and abbess of Las Huelgas in 1220, a very powerful woman.

name: Pope Innocent III
description: Pope who wrote in 1210 trying to stop the abbess of Las Huelgas from preaching and hearing confessions.

name: Héloïse
description: Famous nun, disappointed lover of Peter Abelard, prioress at Argenteuil and abbess of the Paraclete.

name: Peter Abelard
description: Scholar of the University of Paris, tutor and secret husband of Héloïse, sent disgraced to a monastery.

name: Canon Fulbert
description: Canon of Notre Dame and uncle of Héloïse who hired Abelard as her tutor.

name: Christina of Markyate
description: Noble Anglo-Saxon girl from Huntingdon who vowed virginity and resisted her forced marriage to Burthred.

name: Burthred
description: Young man betrothed and married to Christina of Markyate, who refused him.

name: Hildegard of Bingen
description: Example of a strong, influential female religious famed as a scholar and mystic.

name: Caesarius of Arles
description: Author of the first regulations specifically for nuns in the early sixth century.

name: John Cassian
description: Early writer whose works inspired the first rules for nuns.

name: Elijah
description: Prophet whose well lies on Mount Carmel.

name: Saint Francis
description: Founder of the Franciscan movement, whose followers are the strongest new spiritual development.

name: Isabelle the Beautiful
description: Living Covenant character who could be modified into a covenant religious.

name: Curious Nun
description: Example character from Realms of Power: The Divine who could join a covenant as a refugee.

name: Cunfin
description: Covenant hidden in a regio at a Cistercian monastery in Champagne, France.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The game setting whose religious life the chapter describes.

name: Llanthony Priory
description: Welsh priory whose orchard extends over twelve acres.

name: Saint Gall
description: Alpine monastery with just thirteen trees among its graves.

name: Bury Saint Edmunds
description: Great English abbey in Suffolk controlling over 150 manors and fifty knights; King John intervened in its election in 1210.

name: England
description: Kingdom with some seven hundred monasteries in 1220 holding one fifth of the nation's wealth.

name: Wales
description: Region where Llanthony Priory lies.

name: Rome
description: Seat of the pope, where rival abbot candidates seek confirmation.

name: Sempringham
description: Place in Lincolnshire where the Gilbertines were founded in 1130.

name: Fontrevrault
description: Abbey founded in 1100 by Robert of Arbrissel in the Forest of Bart, Anjou; a double house headed by an abbess and royal burial place.

name: Forest of Bart
description: Forest in Anjou where Fontrevrault was founded.

name: Anjou
description: Region of Fontrevrault, tied to the royal family of Aquitaine and Anjou.

name: Amesbury
description: English daughter house of Fontrevrault founded by Henry II.

name: Las Huelgas
description: Richest nunnery under the Cistercian Rule, near Burgos, founded in 1187; royal burial place.

name: Burgos
description: Castilian diocese near Las Huelgas.

name: Palencia
description: Castilian diocese exceptional regarding nunnery chaplains.

name: Castile
description: Kingdom of Alfonso VIII.

name: Coldingham
description: Double foundation burned down on account of the nuns' vanity.

name: University of Paris
description: Young university where Peter Abelard taught.

name: Notre Dame
description: Church in Paris of which Fulbert was a canon.

name: Argenteuil
description: Nunnery where Héloïse was prioress.

name: The Paraclete
description: Nunnery where Héloïse was abbess.

name: Huntingdon
description: English town where Christina of Markyate was born.

name: Champagne
description: Region of France where the covenant of Cunfin lies.

name: Flanders
description: Region where the beguine movement began and many mystics live.

name: Beguinage of Saint Elizabeth
description: Very substantial beguinage in Ghent enclosed by ditches and a wall.

name: Ghent
description: City of the beguinage of Saint Elizabeth.

name: Mount Carmel
description: Mountain in the Holy Land where Carmelite hermits live in caves around Elijah's well.

name: Holy Land
description: Region where the Carmelite Order originated.

name: Jerusalem
description: Seat of the papal legate who approved the Carmelite rule.

name: Provence
description: Region where Augustinian canons staff cathedrals and penitents are called bizzoche.

name: Bavaria
description: Region where Augustinian canons staff many cathedrals.

name: Italy
description: Northern Italy is where the penitent movement began.

name: Germany
description: Region with many mystics and early beguines.

name: France
description: Kingdom where the Trinitarians were founded in 1198.
